title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive
description: Do you have old magazines, vintage zines, or leftover craft supplies? We are gathering materials for a community Collage Poetry project that will be turned into a public exhibition. What is Collage Poetry? Collage Poetry weaves together existing text and visual fragments such as magazine cutouts, newspaper snippets, book jackets, zines, school reports/papers, and even non-paper materials (yarn, ribbon, glitter) to form a new, layered work of art. Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... London: printed by the author, 1671. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

description: Learn how to secure SBIR funding with expert guidance on eligibility, proposal strategy, agencies, and submission tips. ​Join the Office of Innovation and Commercialization (OIC) and The Brink SBDC for a hybrid Info & Advising Session designed to demystify Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) funding. ​This workshop is offered through a partnership between UC San Diego's Office of Innovation and Commercialization and The Brink SBDC at the University of San Diego. Listen to experienced SBIR proposal writers, learn tips and tricks for your first submission, and get answers to your burning questions about the complex world of SBIR grants. Learn about the different parts of a proposal, how to navigate different agencies to maximize your funding, and eligibility requirements. The session is ideal for researchers, faculty, and entrepreneurs who have started— or are considering starting— an innovative company. No prior SBIR experience is required. ​Attendees Will: ​Follow live walkthroughs for finding new funding opportunities ​Understand the legal requirements to receive an SBIR ​Structure their research for SBIR program requirements ​Topics Covered: ​Federal agencies offering SBIR grants ​SBIR Phases and funding amounts ​Corporate formation and legal considerations ​Proposal structure, key sections, and pre-submission strategy ​Featured Speakers: ​Jacques Chirazi, Senior Director of Programs (OIC, UC San Diego) ​Dr. Natalie Castellana, Founder/CEO Abterra Bio | UC San Diego 2012 ​Dr. Stephen Chang, NCI SBIR Reviewer, CGT Pioneer (The Brink @ USD) ​Dr. Pilgrim Jackson, Founder/CEO Yatiri Bio | Informatics & Proteomics ​Dr. Gregory Tudryn, Grantwriter ($90M), NIH/NSF SBIR Reviewer ​Choose your experience: ​In-Person: Join us at the Design & Innovation Building, The Basement for a more a hands-on experience. Limited spots available – register early! ​Virtual: Tune in from anywhere. Register now to get the Zoom link. ​Register now to secure your spot! Those attending virtually will receive a Zoom link upon registration. ​ ​Directions ​For those attending in-person, this event is located at the Basement (Room 151) in the Design and Innovation Building (DIB). The building entrances are located across from the Structural Materials and Engineering building or next to the UC San Diego Central Campus Station bus and trolley stop. ​Learn more about getting to the DIB, including parking, directions, and maps.

description: He was the funniest man in the room. And the most unfiltered. North Coast Repertory Theatre presents the West Coast Premiere of Good Night, Oscar, Pulitzer Prize winner Doug Wright's compassionate and wickedly funny portrait of Oscar Levant — pianist, actor, composer, and legendary wit whose sharp tongue was matched only by his profound musical genius. Set during a fateful 1958 appearance on The Jack Paar Show, this electrifying play captures one unforgettable night in the life of Hollywood's most neurotic and uncensored personality: a tortured artist wrestling with mental illness, addiction, and the price of fame, yet never losing his capacity for devastating honesty and breathtaking artistry. On Broadway, Sean Hayes won the 2023 Tony Award for Best Actor in a Play for his performance as Levant. Equal parts comedy and tragedy, Good Night, Oscar is a love letter to the golden age of television and a showcase for theatrical virtuosity — the story of a man performing himself for an audience, decades before the internet made everyone do it.

It was named a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize® for Drama.

Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... title: India's Platform Economy: Is It Working for Workers?
description: Join us for a conversation unpacking India's new Code on Social Security, 2020, its impact on gig and platform work, and what this landmark policy means in practice. The new framework took effect in November 2025, formally extending labor protections to gig and platform workers for the first time. Key changes include Aadhaar-linked IDs, portable benefits, and mandatory aggregator contributions to a social security fund. The discussion will examine the policy’s implications for India’s rapidly growing gig economy: Can meaningful social protection be provided without undermining platform flexibility? Will the cost of compliance affect the sector’s ability to scale, and ultimately, who will bear that cost? Arti Ahuja, former Union labor secretary when the code was proposed, will offer an inside perspective on how the policy took shape, while Prajna Khanna will bring an investor’s perspective on India’s gig economy and its evolving policy landscape. The discussion will be moderated by professor Achyuta Adhvaryu from the UC San Diego School of Global Policy and Strategy.

title: San Diego Tijuana International Jazz Festival
description: SDTJ Jazz responds to political and trade frictions between the US and Mexico withprogramming that highlights the cooperative cultural expression arising from the inextricablyentwined region. “I think that being on the border is probably the most interesting thing aboutSan Diego,” Daniel Atkinson, SDTJ Jazz founder and executive director, told Downbeatmagazine. “That positions us in a very different way even from a place like Los Angeles.”Bouncing back and forth across the border each day, SDTJ Jazz opens Thursday, Oct. 1 indowntown San Diego at Quartyard with a three-band “Jazz Party.” The program begins with theBinational Youth Ensemble, a group featuring rising high school musicians from the Young LionsJazz Conservatory and Instituto Contemporáneo de Música de Baja California. The program alsoincludes the San Diego debut of rising Tijuana jazz band Colectivo Fronterizo with Baja rapperFémina Fatal and the incendiary Southern California TropiFunk combo Jungle Fire.A new addition this year, Friday, Oct. 2 brings an evening of free performances focusing onTijuana artists on the historic Avenida Revolución at Calle 4ta. The program features popularjazz-rock fusion trio Señales Selañes, Colectivo Fronterizo, and conguero Charlie Chávez.The action then moves back north across the border on Saturday, Oct. 3 for the festival’smarquee event at the California Center for the Arts, Escondido. The day features threeticketed concerts on the main festival stage in the Concert Hall with headliners Danilo Pérez andthe SDSU Jazz Ensembles, the Mingus Dynasty septet, and Brian Blade and the FellowshipBand (ticketed admission $45-$55-$75). Two additional free outdoor performances on the Jazzon the Green stage include leading cross-border Afro-Cuban combo Charlie Chávez y suAfrotruko and Lucía and the Familia Gutiérrez from Veracruz.With widely expanded food and beverage service including multiple food trucks and bars forall attendees, the festival’s Escondido event also offers a new Premium “Friends of theFestival” option ($125) that includes a hosted bar and elevated farm-to-table dinner withreserved seating next to the outdoor stage.SDTJ Jazz closes Sunday, Oct. 4 back in Tijuana on Avenida Revolución at Calle 5ta with a freeprogram recapping the previous days’ highlights, with the Binational Youth Ensemble, Lucía andthe Familia Gutiérrez, Mingus Dynasty, and Brian Blade and the Fellowship Band, plus DaniloPérez with Ensenada’s La Covacha Big Band.Longtime San Diego jazz presenter Dan Atkinson, whose curation of jazz programming at theAthenaeum Music & Arts Library and UC San Diego has earned him international recognition,spearheaded the festival’s creation with key Mexican partner, electric guitarist/bassist JulianPlascencia, the founder of the Tijuana Jazz & Blues Festival. He’s also owner of Praga Café, a keyTijuana music venue, and of Caesar’s, a keystone of the acclaimed Baja food scene.

title: Reed Timmer
venue: George Van Dusen Theatre at North Shore Center
description: Dr. Reed Timmer is an extreme meteorologist and renowned storm chaser with a PhD in meteorology from the University of Oklahoma, known for intercepting some of the world?s most powerful storms to collect scientific data. Over his career, he has chased more than 1,000 tornadoes and 50 hurricanes, making him one of the few people to pursue both an EF5 tornado and a Category 5 hurricane. He invented the armored ?Dominator? storm-chasing vehicles to gather data from inside severe storms and has pioneered advanced sensor deployment methods using probes, drones, balloons, and rockets. In addition to his field research, Timmer provides real-time storm coverage and safety updates through media platforms while continuing his work with National Geographic and RadarOmega.

description: FITZGERALDS & Skeleton Key Brewery Present:The SPECTRAL SILHOUETTE RADIO SHOW! $12/Seat Reserved TablesThe award-winning (L.A. Webfest 2025s Best Comedy/Adventure Podcast, T.O. Webfest 2025s Best Sound Design) Spectral Silhouette Radio Show is coming to Fitzgeralds Nightclub on October 1st!What is the Spectral Silhouette? Its one part mystery audio drama, one part musical, all parts uh equal parts um private parts whatever, its hilarious! Featuring a full jazz band, an original script and songs, and a twenty-person cast and crew, The Spectral Silhouette is an ambitious production from the Chicagoland area that recreates the magic of pulpy old-time radio shows like The Shadow and blends that stereo stardust with modern sensibilities and humor. Youll laugh! Youll chuckle! Youll guffaw!So, whats it about? Well, a clever but somewhat bumbling detective named Monty Eldritch is shot during an armed robbery. Legally dead for five minutes, he shakes the cold grip of the Grim Reaper with the aid of medical professionals. When he regains consciousness, he finds that he can hear the voice of a deceased mobster named Sil. The two agree to work together to find Sils murderers in exchange for assistance with Montys cases. Aided by his trigger-happy partner, Penny Aster, and otherworldly insights from his ghostly ally, Monty becomes the SpectralSilhouette.Sponsored by Skeleton Key Brewery in Woodridge, Illinois, Silhouette started as a one-off production that grew in size and popularity over the years due to word of mouth. One show a month turned into three sold-out monthly performances, eventually leading to theater debuts around the Midwest and awards from festivals nationwideand a few international ones, too.As of 2026, the show is in its fifth year of sarcastic ghosts, despicable crooks, and randymediums, and theres no better way to celebrate this quinquennium (thats a word, right?) milestone than with an exclusive performance at the legendary Fitzgeralds Nightclub!Kick off spooky season the right way with The Spectral Silhouette Radio Show, live October 1st at one of the oldest nightclubs in the Chicagoland area!Normal and paranormal beware, The Spectral Silhouette will always be there! Exhibition Reception "Off-Screen Space"
description: Presented by the Department of Visual Arts and the Suraj Israni Center for Cinematic Arts at UC San Diego. In collaboration with the Suraj Israni Center for Cinematic Arts, Off-Screen Space includes experimental narrative films, video art, multi-channel video installations and a cinematic performance - all made by artists who reside or created the work on the west coast and in the region. The works in the show exist across every surface of the gallery and expand the experience and expectations of the screen. “Off-screen space” is a term used primarily in cinema that refers to a sensation that the image, sound, action and ideas can move past the edges of the screen. In this exhibition, the screen is simultaneously the object, the suggestion and the idea.

description: Step into a world where love is wild, magic is mischievous, and nothing is quite as it seems. title: Good Night, Oscar
address: 987-D Lomas Santa Fe Drive, Solana Beach, CA, 92075
description: He was the funniest man in the room. And the most unfiltered. North Coast Repertory Theatre presents the West Coast Premiere of Good Night, Oscar, Pulitzer Prize winner Doug Wright's compassionate and wickedly funny portrait of Oscar Levant — pianist, actor, composer, and legendary wit whose sharp tongue was matched only by his profound musical genius. Set during a fateful 1958 appearance on The Jack Paar Show, this electrifying play captures one unforgettable night in the life of Hollywood's most neurotic and uncensored personality: a tortured artist wrestling with mental illness, addiction, and the price of fame, yet never losing his capacity for devastating honesty and breathtaking artistry. On Broadway, Sean Hayes won the 2023 Tony Award for Best Actor in a Play for his performance as Levant. Equal parts comedy and tragedy, Good Night, Oscar is a love letter to the golden age of television and a showcase for theatrical virtuosity — the story of a man performing himself for an audience, decades before the internet made everyone do it.

Declared "one of the best comedies in years" by The New York Times, Oh, Mary! received two Tony Awards including Best Direction of a Play (Sam Pinkleton), Drama League Awards for Outstanding Play and Outstanding Direction of a Play, as well as a special citation from the New York Drama Critics' Circle. It was named a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize for Drama.

title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive
description: Do you have old magazines, vintage zines, or leftover craft supplies? We are gathering materials for a community Collage Poetry project that will be turned into a public exhibition. What is Collage Poetry? Collage Poetry weaves together existing text and visual fragments such as magazine cutouts, newspaper snippets, book jackets, zines, school reports/papers, and even non-paper materials (yarn, ribbon, glitter) to form a new, layered work of art. Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... title: Opportunity Framing with AI
description: Whether you are a student startup with a brand new idea, a small business owner with a side project, or a seasoned business mogul, the Entrepreneur Workshops focus on a variety of topics pertinent to your journey. Sponsored by Pillsbury and hosted by the Office of Innovation and Commercialization’s The Basement, these workshops are open to everyone. We invite you to register for as many sessions as you are interested in! ​Event Description: ​Before you build it, pitch it, or launch it, make sure it’s the right idea. This workshop teaches a repeatable process for identifying and framing meaningful opportunities using Human Insights (HI) amplified by Artificial Intelligence (AI). ​Through practical tools, collaborative exercises, and real-time AI exploration, participants learn how to investigate a problem before jumping to solutions. You’ll examine what you think you know, gather human and AI-supported research, identify the people and perspectives that matter, and translate what you learn into a clear, actionable problem statement. Using HI × AI, you’ll challenge assumptions, uncover new perspectives, and determine which opportunities are worth pursuing before investing time, money, or resources in a solution. ​The result is a more thoughtful way to move from uncertainty to opportunity—with greater clarity, confidence, and purpose. ​Refreshments generously provided by Ike's Sandwiches. About the Speaker: ​Kevin Popović | Founder, The Idea Guy® | /kevinpopovic ​Kevin Popović is The Idea Guy®, a strategist, educator, author, and speaker who helps people identify the right problems, create better ideas, and turn those ideas into meaningful innovation. ​He is the creator of AMPLIFIED!, an approach to innovation that integrates Human Insights (HI) with Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve how people understand problems, make decisions, and create solutions. His work is grounded in a simple principle: human insight provides the context, empathy, judgment, and meaning; AI amplifies our ability to research, explore, create, and refine. Together, HI × AI can make innovation more thoughtful, repeatable, and effective. ​Kevin is also pursuing his doctorate at National University, where his research examines how organizations can integrate HI × AI to improve problem identification and innovation practice. His research explores the human and organizational conditions that influence innovation adoption, implementation, and sustained impact—providing an empirical foundation for the ideas and practices behind AMPLIFIED! ​As the former Education Manager at UC San Diego’s Design Lab, Kevin has taught design and innovation at UC San Diego, developed idea incubators at San Diego State University, and advised organizations ranging from startups to Fortune 500 companies. ​Through keynotes, workshops, courses, and consulting, Kevin helps students, entrepreneurs, leaders, and organizations strengthen their creative confidence and innovation capability—combining what people understand with what AI can amplify to solve problems that matter.

title: Ripe presented by Thalia Hall & Deep Cut with Boys Go To Jupiter
description: Ripe remembers sweating to hell in a basement underneath a Subway sandwich shop, building their very first songs in a concrete cube that smelled like fresh bread. They remember selling their first tickets by hand outside the coffee shop that their friends worked at, holding court like twenty-something impresarios trying to move like 50 tickets to a bar that was willing to let you keep the ticket sales if they kept the bar. In a world where we constantly feel the loving pressure to "tell our story", where so many of our friends that have found success as artists have done it alone, Ripe is using their bio to tell you that at the center of everything is collaboration and community, a friendship that has become a bond as strong as family, a constantly spinning object that cannot be properly captured by any single still photograph. This moment, the two songs already out and the new songs coming, catches the band in a moment of intense joyous swelling energy. Working in dream studios, in a city they spent years trying to take a proper chance on, with a producer that had made albums we loved in our formative years, alongside the closest musical relations we've formed. This is our love letter to complicated nostalgia, to relentless empowering change, to realizing that making dreams come true (just like a crisis) only fully makes sense when it is shared. Joy in the wild unknown let us tell you who we were. Bright blues had us ripped apart so we could start again. What comes next is the band swinging for the fences, all in at the table, risking everything for a shot at feeling connected to you. Thank you for being here. title: Owen Riegling - In The Feeling Tour with Payton Smith
description: 18+ with parent or guardian / www.carolspub.comCanadian country artist and award-winning singer-songwriter Owen Riegling is quickly emerging as one of the genre's most authentic and dynamic new voices. Raised in the farming community of Mildmay, Ontario (pop. 1,200), Riegling pairs small-town soul with a modern, arena-ready edge. After winning the 2022 Boots & Hearts Festival Emerging Artist Competition and signing with Universal Music Canada, Riegling broke through with his platinum-certified hit , "rdquo" -> Old Dirt Roads". His expanded EP-turned-album Bruce County (From The Beginning) earned major recognition, including 2025 CCMA Album of the Year, multiple Country Music of Ontario Awards, and a 2025 Juno Award nomination for Breakthrough Artist of the Year. With more than 165 million global streams, his momentum continues to build. A relentless performer, Riegling has headlined his own shows and supported artists including Brett Young, Jake Owen, Tyler Hubbard, Chase Rice, Tyler Braden, Kashus Culpepper, Dierks Bentley, and more. Life on the road, paired with major personal milestones---including his recent marriage to longtime partner Liv---shaped the emotional core of his new Universal Music Canada/Big Loud album, In The Feeling. Produced in Nashville by Oscar Charles and featuring collaborations with some of the city's most respected songwriters, In The Feeling captures a defining chapter of growth and self-discovery. The project finds Riegling wrestling with identity, distance from home, and the balance between ambition and belonging. Radio hit , "rdquo" -> Taillight This Town" reflects that push-and-pull between leaving and longing, while the highly energetic , "rdquo" -> Love Hate Love" showcases his big-stage energy and evolving confidence. Grounded in family, community, and the values that shaped him, Riegling blends vulnerability with conviction. As his sound matures, so does his sense of self. , "rdquo" -> I'm just making the music that I would want to listen to," Riegling says. , "rdquo" -> I'm not trying to be anybody other than myself." From rural Canada to international stages, Riegling is no longer simply chasing the dream---he is fully stepping into it. It's official: on In The Feeling, Owen Riegling has found himself. Now---it's your turn to find him. This event is 18 and over, anyone under 21 MUST be accompanied by a parent or guardian. title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive
description: Do you have old magazines, vintage zines, or leftover craft supplies? We are gathering materials for a community Collage Poetry project that will be turned into a public exhibition. What is Collage Poetry? Collage Poetry weaves together existing text and visual fragments such as magazine cutouts, newspaper snippets, book jackets, zines, school reports/papers, and even non-paper materials (yarn, ribbon, glitter) to form a new, layered work of art. Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: United States Poet Laureates | Exhibit
description: Explore the works of the U.S. Poet Laureates through selected books and broadsides held in the Archive of New Poetry, a part of UC San Diego Library's Special Collections & Archives. United States Poet Laureates is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Image taken from "A Map to the Next World" by 2019-2022 Poet Laureate Joy Harjo. Harjo was the first Native American Poet Laureate and centered her term on celebrating indigenous poetry and voices with her project "Living Nations, Living Worlds."

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... London: printed by the author, 1671. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: Hoops for the Hub
description: Join us for the 2nd annual Hoops for The Hub, a 3-on-3 basketball tournament and 3-point contest fundraiser taking place October 3-4, 2026, benefiting The Hub Basic Needs Center at UC San Diego. Open to adults 18 and older of all skill levels, the tournament guarantees each team at least three games. More than just a tournament, it’s a high-energy weekend of competitive basketball that brings together students, faculty, staff, and community members to build camaraderie and raise vital funds in support of students facing basic needs challenges. Proceeds from the tournament will help provide students with nutritious, no-cost food, temporary emergency housing, and financial crisis support—ensuring they have the resources needed to focus on their education.

title: Mehregan Fall Fete
description: Join us for a stimulating evening celebrating the Iranian fall festival of Mehregan . Celebration attendees are invited to the Museum’s James S. Copley Auditorium for the annual Mehregan concert at 5:00 p.m. Mehregan sponsors are invited to a special pre-concert tour of the Arts of Iran gallery beginning at 4:00 p.m. Sponsorship packages start at $200. For more information about sponsorship, email Kate Burnite at kburnite@sdmart.org . Concertgoers will enjoy welcome remarks from Roxana Velásquez, Maruja Baldwin Executive Director and CEO of The San Diego Museum of Art, prior to being seated in the Museum’s James S. Copley Auditorium for the annual Mehregan concert at 5:00 p.m. This year’s performance features Rana Mansour . Concert tickets start at $60.54. The Mehregan Fall Fete is a collaboration between The San Diego Museum of Art and the Persian Cultural Center. This annual partnership supports the Arts of Iran gallery and raises funds for acquisitions of art from Iran and the Persianate world or created by contemporary Iranian artists. To purchase tickets, visit pccsd.eventbrite.com .

title: Docent-Led Walks
description: Join us every 1st Saturday of the month for docent-led walks of Scripps Coastal Reserve from 9-11 am! Learn more about the biodiversity and history of this reserve from our knowledgeable docents and staff on a 0.5 mile, mostly flat trail. The last hike departs at 10:30 am. Registration is not required, but participants must sign our waiver onsite. Please reach out at nrs@ucsd.edu if you prefer to sign the waiver electronically in advance. Please keep in mind that there are no water or bathroom facilities at the reserve. Also note that while this event is family-friendly, no pets are allowed inside the reserve.

It is a chance to explore one of the city's most distinctive new museums alongside fellow Tritons and dig into the history of the place we all chose to call home after graduation. The hair products may have changed, but the drama, the rivalries, and the thirst for hallway clout remain timeless. It is the musical you know and love, but dragged through a cloud of strawberry scented vapor and a TikTok filter. It's the show that you want (Ooh! Ooh! Ooh, honey!) title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive
description: Do you have old magazines, vintage zines, or leftover craft supplies? We are gathering materials for a community Collage Poetry project that will be turned into a public exhibition. What is Collage Poetry? Collage Poetry weaves together existing text and visual fragments such as magazine cutouts, newspaper snippets, book jackets, zines, school reports/papers, and even non-paper materials (yarn, ribbon, glitter) to form a new, layered work of art. Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... London: printed by the author, 1671. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

description: Sunday, October 4 6:00 p.m. doors open 6:30 p.m. concert begins The San Diego Museum of Art John M. and Sally B Thornton Rotunda Celebrating the first season of Camarada in residence at SDMA, Poéticas del Arrabal: Opera and Tango transforms the SDMA rotunda into an intimate concert hall where music and visual art resonate together. Poéticas del Arrabal: Opera and Tango explores the expressive world of tango through the music of Astor Piazzolla in arrangements by Andrés Martín. Performed by The Camarada Tango Quartet, together with singers Gabriela Bojórquez and Martín de León, the program brings together the intimacy of chamber music, the dramatic language of opera, and the distinctive voice of tango. More than a concert, the evening explores memory through one of the world’s most expressive musical traditions, inviting audiences to experience longing, nostalgia, and human connection in dialogue with the Museum. Tickets on sale now! Rather than presenting performances only alongside exhibitions, the program invites artists to create in direct conversation with the Museum’s collection, exhibitions, architecture, and public spaces. Experience a full season of music, dance, theater, and family programming with Museum as a Stage at The San Diego Museum of Art. Featured at top right: Photograph of Andrés Martín by Monique Feil. description: 21+ / www.carolspub.comAbout Chris Housman: Chris's musical apprenticeship began very early as he cut his musical teeth playing fiddle and singing country classics with his family band at a Wild West show geared towards tourists visiting Dodge City, , "rdquo" -> The Cowboy Capital of the World." Now based in Nashville, Chris Housman has realized a dream that seemed impossible when he was a young man growing up on a cattle farm a 40-minute drive from Dodge City, Kansas (30 minutes if you know the backroads). His debut album's title track, , "rdquo" -> Blueneck," hit No. 1 on the iTunes country chart, earned praise from Rolling Stone, Billboard, Good Morning America, and The Tennessean, and scored him an nomination for GLAAD's Outstanding Breakthrough Music Artist Award. USA Today praised Chris's strong vocals and , "rdquo" -> rich Southern charm," calling him the , "rdquo" -> gay-me-changer" country music needs right now. Chris's sophomore album, appropriately titled Dodge City, set to release August 28th, is an homage to the place that shaped him, but that he knew he'd ultimately have to leave in order to realize his dreams as a country artist and proud member of the LGBTQ+ community. title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive
description: Do you have old magazines, vintage zines, or leftover craft supplies? We are gathering materials for a community Collage Poetry project that will be turned into a public exhibition. What is Collage Poetry? Collage Poetry weaves together existing text and visual fragments such as magazine cutouts, newspaper snippets, book jackets, zines, school reports/papers, and even non-paper materials (yarn, ribbon, glitter) to form a new, layered work of art. Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

Image taken from "A Map to the Next World" by 2019-2022 Poet Laureate Joy Harjo. title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... London: printed by the author, 1671. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

Attendees will experience the unique format of practicing mindfulness alongside scholars, who then present their research in a reflective, inspirational symposium. Following the presentations, a panel Q&A will offer opportunities for meaningful dialogue. Our aspiration is to support you in deepening your mindfulness practice while offering profound insights into how Buddhist wisdom and scientific discovery can unite to create lasting solutions for the world. title: Cancer Therapeutics Training (CT2) Talks | Michael Bouvet, MD, FACS
description: Development of Imaging Probes for Fluorescence Guided Surgery of GI and Endocrine Tumors Michael Bouvet, MD, is a board-certified surgical oncologist and professor of surgery specializing in endocrine and gastrointestinal cancers. He serves as director of Endocrine Surgery and co-director of the Gastrointestinal Cancer Unit at UC San Diego Health, with expertise in thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreatic, esophageal and other gastrointestinal cancers. A physician-scientist, Dr. Bouvet focuses his research on fluorescence-guided surgery and tumor-specific imaging to improve the detection and removal of cancer during surgery. His work includes developing fluorescent probes for the early detection of colon and pancreatic cancers and techniques to help identify nerves during thyroid surgery. He earned his medical degree from the University of Washington, completed his general surgery residency at UC San Diego and fellowship training in surgical oncology at MD Anderson Cancer Center. He joined UC San Diego Health in 1998.

description: Please Note: There is a delivery delay on all orders until approximately two days prior to the show. Based in Los Angeles, bunii is a self-produced artist who has become a prominent figure in the underground scene. After starting his career as a producer at age 15, he transitioned into a solo artist in 2023, eventually finding breakout viral success with his 2024 single , "rdquo" -> SAINT." To date, bunii has amassed 170M+ global streams, including 119.3M+ U.S. streams, alongside 1.7M+ video views and a combined social following of 133K

title: Paris Chansons
description: Paris Chansons is an exciting French band with an Eastern European gypsy twist! They are known for their original renditions of French favorites from Charles Aznavour, Joe Dassin, Edith Piaf, Macias, Adamo, Dalida, all the way to contemporary artists like Zaz. Their exhilarating performances are punctuated with gypsy jazz standards as well as classics in Russian, Italian, and other languages. Three multilingual singers bring an unparalleled diversity to their shows. Julia Kantor, originally from the Ukraine, lived and studied in France where she discovered in French music a soul connection that still imbues every performance. She entrances from the stage with a sultry voice and dynamic presence. Together with her husband, Jacob, a Russian-born singer/songwriter, they launched Paris Chansons. Max Cohen grew up in Morocco steeped in French music, particularly the songs of Enrico Macias. Maxs rich velvety tone delivers beautifully nuanced renditions of his favorites, complete with a signature North African lilt. Superb musicianship anchors the ensemble, effortlessly moving from jazzy improvisation to slow-burning balladry to blistering gypsy fervor. All seasoned pros, the musicians are Jeff Lams on piano, Adam Cohen on upright bass, Endre Balogh on violin, Sinclair Lott on drums and Jacob Kantor on guitar. Paris Chansons takes you an a journey without leaving your seat (except, of course, to dance!), a spectacular celebration of French and international music that brings the world that much closer. title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive
description: Do you have old magazines, vintage zines, or leftover craft supplies? We are gathering materials for a community Collage Poetry project that will be turned into a public exhibition. What is Collage Poetry? Collage Poetry weaves together existing text and visual fragments such as magazine cutouts, newspaper snippets, book jackets, zines, school reports/papers, and even non-paper materials (yarn, ribbon, glitter) to form a new, layered work of art. Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... London: printed by the author, 1671. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: Book Launch: The Zoo Lady by Dr. Sandra E. Bonura
address: 1649 El Prado, Suite #3, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: The Zoo Lady: The Forgotten Legend Who Saved & Then Built The San Diego Zoo She was a middle-aged, divorced mother who became the world’s first female zoo director and the first woman to lead the National Zoo Association (AZA)—so why has history forgotten her name? While Harry Wegeforth was the founder, it was Belle Benchley who ensured the San Diego Zoo survived its darkest days. In 1925, she took a temporary bookkeeping job at the struggling four-year-old zoo—a position she admittedly ‘dreaded’—only to stay for thirty years. She didn’t just save a failing institution; she built it into a world-class treasure, reshaping global conservation long before Jane Goodall or Dian Fossey. From wrestling rattlesnakes to orchestrating the historic cross-country giraffe trek that inspired the bestseller West with Giraffes, Benchley was a “leader of steel” who broke the glass ceiling. Join award-winning author and historian Dr. Sandra E. Bonura for a journey through rare archival images as she uncovers how this unlikely pioneer transformed a struggling local park into a global icon. Book Signing & Special Offer: Copies of Dr. Bonura’s brand-new book, The Zoo Lady: How Belle Benchley Built the San Diego Zoo, will be autographed and available for purchase at a special author’s discount. Program ticket includes lunch

title: Malcolm Todd: Do That Again Tour (MOVED TO THE SALT SHED OUTDOORS)
description: When Malcolm Todd graduated high school in 2022, he told his parents he would be taking a gap year to pursue music. They, unsurprisingly, were less than thrilled by the proclamation, but gave him a year to see if it could work. They learned what the rest of the music industry quickly realized: never bet against Malcolm Todd. ?Every single day since I told my mom I wanted to do this, I have actively worked to grow my fanbase, to get better at music, to build this world,? he explains. By the time he shared Sweet Boy in 2024, his day job at Cold Stone was in the rearview. Tracks like ?Roommates? were racking up millions of streams daily. Fast forward a year, and Todd is more motivated than ever on his self-titled album, a declaration that he isn?t a hype machine or a flash in the pan, but a generation-defining voice.

Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. title: El Niño and San Diego: What to Expect
description: ​NOAA is forecasting that the coming El Niño could be among the strongest on record. UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography has a long history of researching, tracking and understanding El Niño events and impacts. For San Diego Climate Week, Scripps Institution of Oceanography is bringing together a group of leading experts to talk about the science of El Niño, the latest technology scientists are deploying to track and detect this event, and the potential impacts to San Diego — from shifts in weather to effects on our ocean ecosystems and coastlines. Scientists will also share information on El Niño connections to climate change and how the event is giving society a look into our climate future. ​Melissa Carter: Biological Oceanographer and Manager of the Shore Stations Program at UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography ​Mark Gold: Environmental Scientist and Director of California Cooperative Oceanic Fisheries Investigations (CalCOFI) at UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography ​Julie Kalansky: Climate Scientist and Deputy Director of Operations for the Center for Western for Weather and Water Extremes at UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography ​Daniel Rudnick: Physical Oceanographer and Director of the Instrument Development Group at UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography ​Adam Young: Coastal Geomorphologist at UC San Diego’s Scripps Institution of Oceanography

title: Distinguished Scientist Director’s Lecture Series | Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH, FASCO
description: Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer: Understanding the Rise Dr. Kimmie Ng is a Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School, Associate Chief of the Division of Gastrointestinal Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (DFCI), and the FoundingDirector of the Young-Onset Colorectal Cancer Center at DFCI. Her research focuses on identifying dietary and molecular predictors of colorectal cancer risk and survival, with a special interest in the vitamin D pathway, microbiome, and young-onset colorectal cancer. She has led multiple clinical trials of novel therapies for patients with colorectal cancer, and is the recipient of numerous NIH, foundation, and industry grants. She chaired the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) Scientific Program Committee for the 2023 Annual Meeting and currently serves as a member of ASCO’s Nominating Committee. She was appointed an Associate Editor of JAMA (Journal of the American Medical Association) in February 2024. She has been featured in multiple national media outlets, including the TODAY Show, ABC News, The New York Times, and CNN to raise awareness of young-onset colorectal cancer and the importance of cancer screening, and she was selected for inclusion in The Washington Post Next 50, a list ofpeople shaping society in 2026. Dr. Ng obtained her Bachelor of Science degree with Distinction from Yale University and her Doctor of Medicine degree as a 21st Century Scholar from theUniversity of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine. She completed a residency in internal medicine at University of California, San Francisco (UCSF) and a medical oncology fellowship at Dana-Farber/Partners Cancer Care. She subsequently received a Master of Public Health degree from Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.

title: Wings Over Water
description: Across the heartland of North America, a wetland kingdom of connected rivers, lakes, and waterways has provided an oasis for wildlife since the retreat of the last ice age over 10,000 years ago. Today, these water highways are home to countless species. Alongside herds of bison in the Great Plains and salamanders in the smallest ponds, millions of frequent fliers rely on this pristine wilderness for survival. Wings Over Water, narrated by Michael Keaton, follows three magnificent bird species—the Sandhill Crane, the Yellow Warbler, and the Mallard Duck—as they migrate along these epic “flyways.” With extraordinary footage brought to life on the Heikoff Giant Dome IMAX® screen, audiences can fly alongside these incredible birds and experience the wonder of one of North America’s most diverse and untouched ecosystems.

title: Henry Carpender Quartet w/ special guest Chris Greene LIVE IN THE SIDEBAR!
description: FITZGERALDS SIDEBAR Presents: Henry Carpender Quartet w/ special guest Chris Greene FREE SHOW! RESERVATION AVAILABLE! Henry Carpender is a trombonist, composer, and educator based in the city of Chicago. An artist who is equally informed by his classical training, love of Jazz, and childhood playing rock music (primarily with his father John Carpender), Henry's playing and writing is a charming blend of punchy, sensitive, quirky, and dripping with love for life and self expression. Henry's dedication to music making began at age 13 when he played his first gig with the much beloved local band Expo '76. Since then, through both his education and the beginning of his professional freelance career, Henry has been fortunate enough to share the stage with Dag Juhlin, Billy Harper, Robbie Fulks, Tanya Darby, Cathy Richardson, NRBQ and the Canadian Brass. Henry has also enjoyed a healthy start to a career as a private instructor and group music educator, running a small studio of dedicated middle and high schoolers across the Chicagoland area. When he's not playing or teaching, he can be found playing video games, cooking a new dish, or relaxing on Montrose beach. This show will be an opportunity to premiere new work, revisit some favorites, and share arrangements of some of Henry's favorite artists. Aval Stanley on the Keys, Jesse Lear on Bass, and Tommy Sagins on Drums, and featuring Chris Greene on Tenor Saxophone Grab dinner before the show at BABYGOLD BARBECUE ***PARKING*** There is rather limited street parking in the area, we recommend arriving by rideshare, bicycle, or rickshaw. ***AGE RESTRICTIONS*** ALL AGES!
