Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. London: printed by the author, 1671. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: San Diego Startup Week at UC San Diego
description: Learn more: https://sandiegostartupweek.org/ Join us at the Design and Innovation Building on 11/4 as we celebrate San Diego Startup Week's UC San Diego day! San Diego Startup Week (SDSW) returns for its 14th year, bringing together 5,000+ founders, talent, investors, builders, and operators for five days of igniting connections, accelerating learning, and fueling innovation. This year's SDSW theme, Where Startups Take Off, bridges the fundamentals every founder needs — community, capital, craft, and courage — with the daring vision of what comes next. At the convergence of life sciences, defense, AI, and tech, the breakthroughs happening in San Diego today will shape global markets tomorrow. SDSW is your early access to all of it. Registration is now live for all ticket types. Secure your spot before liftoff to unlock access to: Keynotes and fireside chats Networking and mentorship Expert panels and workshops Pitch competitions and startup expos Live demos and more SDSW is where co-founders meet, companies find their runway, and the right introduction changes everything. Sessions at UC San Diego include: Funding Remix Wednesday, November 4 · 1:00 PM to 1:45 PM This founder-focused session breaks down the real-world funding paths available to startups—from bootstrapping and loans to angels, venture capital, and corporate or strategic partners. We’ll unpack the pros, cons, tradeoffs, and “what nobody tells you” of each option, then challenge conventional thinking about how—and when—to raise. Come with questions, leave with a broader funding toolkit, sharper questions, and fresh ideas for financing your next move. ESET Cybersecurity Workshop Wednesday, November 4 · 1:00 PM to 1:45 PM San Diego Startup Expo Wednesday, November 4 · 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM The San Diego Startup Expo showcases the region’s boldest startups, top resource partners, and the organizations fueling what’s next. Meet the founders turning San Diego’s best ideas into real businesses. Connect with the accelerators, investors, and support networks powering their growth. Talk to the teams hiring for their next chapter. This is San Diego’s innovation ecosystem, unfiltered and in person. Perfect YOUR Investor Pitch: Pitch Deconstruction Powered by San Diego & Imperial SBDC Wednesday, November 4 · 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM You’ve only got one shot do not miss your chance to flow….this opportunity comes once in a Startup Week yo. Bring your 4 minute investor pitch and join the SBDC team for a deep, hands-on session where you’ll discover the anatomy of an outstanding investor pitch. And then the fun begins! You will be delivering YOUR investor pitch at least 3 times and receiving feedback and we deconstruct and reconstruct your investor pitches live in the session. This is not for the faint of heart so be sure to bring your computer and come prepared to work it! Come curious. Leave connected. Startup Advising Powered by San Diego & Imperial SBDC Wednesday, November 4 · 1:00 PM to 5:00 PM Every year the San Diego & Imperial SBDC provides entrepreneurs with 800+ trainings and more than 19,000 hours of 1:1 advising free of charge. Since 2022, we are thrilled to have helped entrepreneurs in our region create a $2B+ impact on the local economy by supporting them from Idea to Exit and everything in between! The San Diego & Imperial SBDC is bringing its powerhouse team to Startup Week for the second year in a row support fierce founders building the their businesses. Here are some of the areas that SBDC’s advisors at Startup Week can help you: • Business start and launch strategy • Business Strategy • Debt Financing • High-Growth/Scaling • Human Resources • Marketing Strategy, planning and execution • Branding • Sales Growth • Retail Sales • B2B Sales • Government & Corporate Contracting • Small Business Certifications (minority owned, women owned, etc.) Sign up for a 30 min 1:1 advising appointment and move YOUR business forward! Startup Week appointments will open for soon! Keynote ft. Daniel Marashlian, Co-Founder & CTO at Drata Wednesday, November 4 · 2:00 PM to 3:00 PM How Drata validated its business and technology idea before scaling into a $2B unicorn startup company. Pitch Pulse Grand Finale & Showcase Wednesday, November 4 · 3:00 PM to 8:00 PM The Pitch Pulse Grand Finale & Showcase is the culminating in-person event of the Pitch Pulse startup series, taking place during Startup San Diego Week. Throughout the year, Pitch Pulse runs multiple vertical pitch sessions across different sectors, selecting top-performing early-stage startups from each round to advance to this final showcase in San Diego. The event features live pitches from a curated group of startups across emerging technology areas including AI, biotech, defense, maritime, and other frontier technologies, alongside members of the broader innovation ecosystem. Held in collaboration with Startup World Cup, the Final Showcase connects selected startups from across the U.S. with the San Diego ecosystem, creating a high-signal environment for visibility, feedback, and connection. Startup Stories: From Concept to Millions in Revenue Wednesday, November 4 · 3:00 PM to 3:45 PM Grayson Lafrenz, Founder and CEO of Cadre AI, shares his journey as a serial entrepreneur—from building a global tech-enabled marketing firm to leading the charge in AI enablement with his latest venture. Learn what inspired Grayson to build these companies, how he overcame challenges along the way, how he built a strong team culture while delivering phenomenal business results, and what it took to grow from a bootstrapped startup to generating millions in revenue. Post-Exit Founder (PEF) SDSW Mixer Wednesday, November 4 · 5:30 PM to 8:00 PM ​Join us for a private event filled with founders that have exited their business and exit-curious founders for an evening focused on launching and scaling. ​Complimentary drinks and appetizers will be available. ​Spots are limited and it will fill up quickly. ​For post-exit founders, this is a chance to stay close to the edge by engaging with founders approaching the same transition you’ve already made. Share your perspective, help others avoid costly mistakes, and meet future collaborators, co-investors, or partners before they cross over.

title: Bridging Biomedical Breakthroughs Summit: AI in Biomedical Innovation
description: UC San Diego School of Biological Sciences 4th Bridging Biomedical Breakthroughs Summit AI in Biomedical Innovation: Accelerating Discovery in Therapeutics, Diagnostics, and Imaging Date: Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026Time: 1:00-6:30 p.m.Location: UC San Diego campus; exact location TBDArtificial intelligence is transforming how biomedical discoveries are made, translated, and delivered. The School of Biological Sciences 4th Bridging Biomedical Breakthroughs Summit brings together faculty innovators, entrepreneurs, investors, legal experts, and healthcare leaders to explore how AI is accelerating the future of biomedical innovation. Hosted by the School of Biological Sciences in partnership with the Office of Innovation and Commercialization and the School of Medicine, this Summit will spotlight emerging advances in therapeutics, diagnostics, and medical imaging, highlighting how AI is enabling new approaches to discovery, improving precision, and accelerating the path from scientific insight to real-world impact. Open to UC San Diego faculty, postdocs, and students, as well as leaders across the medical, healthcare, and life sciences industries, the Summit will feature insights from successful entrepreneurs and investors shaping the future of AI-enabled biomedical innovation. Attendees will gain perspectives on launching and scaling companies, advancing research toward translation, and navigating the path from discovery to impact. The program will also feature faculty innovation pitches showcasing groundbreaking research and emerging technologies that harness AI with the potential to transform therapeutics, diagnostics, and medical imaging. Join us for an engaging afternoon of cutting-edge science, cross-sector perspectives, and meaningful connections at the intersection of biology, technology, and innovation.

title: New Writing Series: Yaryna Chornohuz and Amelia Glaser
description: About New Writing Series UC San Diego’s New Writing Series invites local, national, and international authors to read and perform throughout the academic year. Welcoming a wide range of authors and genres, including playwrights, poets, translators, essayists, critics, fiction writers, and performance artists, the New Writing Series celebrates both emerging and established award-winning writers. Readers also include Department of Literature faculty and graduate students in the MFA Program in Writing. The readings are followed by in-depth question and answer periods that center on craft and artistic practice. The New Writing Series is co-sponsored by the Department of Literature and the UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. Recordings of New Writing Series readings, as well as its predecessor, the New Poetry Series, which dates back to 1972, are part of the Archive for New Poetry in UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. This New Writing Series event features readings from Yaryna Chornohuz and Amelia Glaser. Yaryna Chornohuz Born in Kyiv, Ukraine, Yaryna Chornohuz is a writer, a poet, and a sergeant in the Ukrainian Marine Corps. She first volunteered for Ukraine's defense effort in 2019 as a combat medic. She later joined the Marines and retrained as a drone pilot. As a service member, she has been awarded the medals For Saving a Life, For Military Service to Ukraine, and the Badge of Honor of the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine. Chornohuz is the author of three poetry collections – How the War Circle Bends (2020), [dasein: defense of presence] (2023), and Nobody’s Saffron (2025). Her first nonfiction book, documenting six years of her experience as a female combatant in Russia's war against Ukraine, is forthcoming in Ukrainian. She was awarded Ukraine's highest literary distinction, the Taras Shevchenko National Prize (2024), for [dasein: defense of presence], as well as the UN Women in Arts Award (2024). Her poetry has been translated into English, French, German, Polish, and other languages. She is a member of PEN Ukraine. Amelia Glaser is a Professor of Literature at UCSD, and a translator from Ukrainian, Yiddish, and Russian. She is the author of Jews and Ukrainians in Russia’s Literary Borderlands (2012) and Songs in Dark Times: Yiddish Poetry of Struggle from Scottsboro to Palestine (2020). Her translations and co-translations from Ukrainian include books by Halyna Kruk, Iya Kiva, and Yaryna Chornohuz. Her translations of Chornohuz's [dasein] and Nobody’s Saffron have appeared, respectively, with Jantar (2025) and Arrowsmith (2026). Our events are FREE and open to the public!

Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: Spinning Resistance: Women, Cloth, and the Long Memory of 1776
address: 1649 El Prado, Suite #3, San Diego, CA, 92101
description: The spinning wheel keeps showing up at moments of political crisis — and it’s never just about spinning. In the 1760s, American women turned spinning bees into public acts of resistance against British taxation. Arts and Crafts reformers claimed it as a rebuke to industrial capitalism. In the 1920s, Gandhi made the charkha the emblem of Indian independence from the British Empire. Twentieth-century American women, meanwhile, rediscovered it as a symbol of a revolutionary female tradition the original 1776 had denied them — decorating their homes with it, wearing the loose clothing it evoked, claiming the Daughters of Liberty as their own foremothers. But the spinning wheel casts a longer shadow: enslaved women spun and wove too, and the cotton that fed industrial production had been harvested by coerced labor for generations. Join the San Diego History Center for another program in our America at 250 series as historian Molly McClain explores the history of the spinning wheel across three continents and 150 years to ask what commemorative culture commemorates — and who gets to decide. Molly McClain (PhD, Yale) is a professor of history at the University of San Diego. Her research focuses on women’s history, philanthropy, and cultural history more broadly. A ninth-generation San Diegan, she is the author of four books and numerous articles, including Ellen Browning Scripps: New Money and American Philanthropy (2017). McClain’s public history work includes over a decade as editor of The Journal of San Diego History and the successful designation of the La Jolla Park Coastal Historic District to the National Register of Historic Places in 2024. title: Run Ri (潤日): China's New Emigrants to Japan and the Anti-Foreigner Backlash
venue: School of Global Policy and Strategy
description: Japan is undergoing a little-noticed demographic shift: a growing influx of Chinese entrepreneurs, intellectuals and education-focused families relocating for stability. Drawing on years of reporting from Tokyo, GPS alumnus and journalist Takehiro Masutomo examines the rise of this "Run Ri" movement and what it means for a country long defined by its relative homogeneity. From surging property purchases and competition for elite schools to Chinese-language bookstores and exiled intellectuals, Tokyo is emerging as a new hub for the Chinese diaspora – leading some to call it the “next Hong Kong.” But this growing presence has also fueled unease and anti-foreigner rhetoric. Masutomo's reporting brought this overlooked population into public view and helped to ignite a national debate in Japan that has contributed to tighter visa policies. He explores the tension between economic necessity and cultural anxiety shaping Japan's immigration debate. Speaker: Takehiro Masutomo, Author and Independent Journalist; Yale World Fellow Moderator: Margaret Roberts, Director, 21st Century China Center: Co-director, China Data Lab, UC San Diego School of Global Policy and Strategy; Professor, UC San Diego Department of Political Science ------------------ This public lecture is organized by the 21st Century China Center (21CCC) at the UC San Diego School of Global Policy and Strategy. title: Hesiod's Body Sublime: Metabolic Aesthetics in the Hesiodic Corpus
description: The archaic Greek poet, Hesiod, gives us bodies. Godly bodies that consume other gods. Mortal bodies that digest godly gifts. Bodies that amaze, disgust, and turn breath into poetry. This talk interrogates the bodies of the Hesiodic corpus especially for their metabolic capacities and how metabolism defines political and poetic success. Speaker Bio: Stephen A. Sansom is an assistant professor in the Department of Classics at Florida State University. His research investigates Greek epic poetry from literary, computational and comparativist perspectives. His first monograph project, The Hesiodic Shield of Heracles and the Aesthetics of Olympus (under review) situates the Shield of Heracles in the politicized aesthetics of Hesiod’s cosmos. His second book project, Patterns of Expectancy in Greek Epic, uses data science and close reading to explore the meanings generated by the metrical position of words over the thousand-year history of Greek hexameter poetry. His work has been supported by fellowships from the N.E.H., Harvard University’s C.H.S. (Washington, D.C.), and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens. He currently serves on the Advisory Board of the new FSU Humanities Center, which seeks to promote and advance the humanities through fellowships, conferences, and conversation. title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive

What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. title: Weed Warriors
description: Join us every Friday for weeding/work parties at Scripps Coastal Reserve from 8-10 am! Learn more about the flora and fauna of the reserve while lending a hand to remove invasive plants. No RSVP required, but must be able to sign a waiver upon arrival. Make sure to wear closed-toed shoes and clothes you don't mind getting dirty. Gloves and tools will be provided. Please keep in mind that there are no water or bathroom facilities at the reserve. Also note that while this event is family-friendly, no dogs or other pets are allowed inside the reserve.

title: UCSD/SDSU Fall 2026 Software Carpentries Workshop
description: The UCSD Library, Research IT Services, and SDSU Research Cyberinfrastructure are teaming up to host a FREE, four-half-day Software Carpentries Workshop for our campus research communities! Designed specifically for novice to intermediate learners, this hands-on bootcamp will help you level up your research efficiency through foundational computing tools. What You'll Learn: The Unix Shell: Automate repetitive tasks and manage files effortlessly. Git Version Control: Track script changes and collaborate seamlessly. Python Programming: Write clean code to analyze, manipulate, and visualize your data. No prior coding experience required—our Carpentries-certified instructors provide a supportive environment to get you comfortable with digital research tools.

title: Felt Together
description: Inspired by the intricate bas-relief needlework and cozy scenes featured in My Bed: Enchanting Ways to Fall Asleep Around the World , our newest Together workshop series, Felt Together , explores the art of needle felting. The series is led by Sophie Ancel, a fiber artist who blends rich textures and thoughtful layering to bring imaginative landscapes to life. Through her process-driven approach to wool and textile art, she brings a warm, accessible perspective to the world of living craft. Friday, November 6, 2026 | 5-7pm In November, create a night sky scene out of wool. Sophie will teach you how to layer and mix colorful fibers to build a cozy scene with glowing windows, trees, and stars. The Together series at Mingei invites makers of all skill levels to come together and create in a supportive, low-pressure environment. Past iterations— Sew Together, Weave Together , Dye Together , Stitch Together , Clay Together, and Knot Together —explore a variety of craft techniques while emphasizing collaboration, experimentation, and hands-on learning. Each workshop encourages participants to connect with materials, try new skills, and enjoy the process of making together.

title: Raza Resource Centro Writing Collective
description: Join the Raza Resource Centro’s Community Writing Collective, a supportive space dedicated to coaching, advising, and mentoring scholars through the writing process. Whether you’re preparing a competitive research abstract, applying to scholarships, fellowships, or internships, or looking to strengthen your academic writing, this collective offers guidance tailored to your goals. Led by our team of Learning Specialists, the program provides one-on-one support and peer collaboration across diverse disciplines including health sciences, humanities, social sciences, and STEM. 📍 Every Friday | 12 PM – 2 PM | Pepper Canyon Hall Level 2, Room 264 - Raza Resource Centro All are welcome to stop by, connect with peers, and take your writing to the next level. For questions, contact Omar Padilla, PhD, Associate Director of Academic Initiatives at o1padilla@ucsd.edu. This event is open to all undergraduate, graduate and professional students, regardless of race, color, national origin, or any other protected status.

title: Line Break: Poetry in the Library
description: Need a creative break? Join us for Line Break: Poetry in the Library, a monthly drop-in series at Geisel Library. We kick things off with 15 minutes of open-mic poetry, offering a welcoming space to share original poetry and spoken word, or to just cheer on your peers. Spend the rest of the hour getting hands-on with activities led by the Library’s curator for Archive for New Poetry, ranging from concrete poetry and zine-making to a hands-on activity searching the library catalog. No registration is required; only your curiosity and creativity are needed. Drop in, take a break and realize the power of poetry. These events support the campus-wide Common Read initiative. title: The Outsiders (Touring)
description: Adapted from S.E. HINTON's seminal novel and FRANCIS FORD COPPOLA's iconic film, this thrilling new musical features a book by ADAM RAPP with JUSTIN LEVINE, music and lyrics by JAMESTOWN REVIVAL (Jonathan Clay & Zach Chance) & Tony Award® winner JUSTIN LEVINE, music supervision, orchestration, & arrangements by JUSTIN LEVINE, choreography by RICK KUPERMAN & JEFF KUPERMAN, & direction by Tony Award® winner DANYA TAYMOR. Entertainment Weekly says, "THE OUTSIDERS has the power to inspire an entire generation." In Tulsa, Oklahoma, 1967, Ponyboy Curtis, his best friend Johnny Cade and their Greaser family of 'outsiders' battle with their affluent rivals, the Socs. THE OUTSIDERS navigates the complexities of self-discovery as the Greasers dream about who they want to become in a world that may never accept them. With a dynamic original score, THE OUTSIDERS is a story of friendship, family, belonging..and the realization that there is still "lots of good in the world."

title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive
description: Do you have old magazines, vintage zines, or leftover craft supplies? We are gathering materials for a community Collage Poetry project that will be turned into a public exhibition. What is Collage Poetry? Collage Poetry weaves together existing text and visual fragments such as magazine cutouts, newspaper snippets, book jackets, zines, school reports/papers, and even non-paper materials (yarn, ribbon, glitter) to form a new, layered work of art. Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. title: New Writing Series: Judith Peraino, Tom Enaney, and Anna Joy Springer
description: About New Writing Series UC San Diego’s New Writing Series invites local, national, and international authors to read and perform throughout the academic year. Welcoming a wide range of authors and genres, including playwrights, poets, translators, essayists, critics, fiction writers, and performance artists, the New Writing Series celebrates both emerging and established award-winning writers. Readers also include Department of Literature faculty and graduate students in the MFA Program in Writing. The readings are followed by in-depth question and answer periods that center on craft and artistic practice. The New Writing Series is co-sponsored by the Department of Literature, Department of Music, and the UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. Recordings of New Writing Series readings, as well as its predecessor, the New Poetry Series, which dates back to 1972, are part of the Archive for New Poetry in UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. This New Writing Series event features readings from Judith Peraino, Tom Enaney, and Anna Joy Springer. Judith A. Peraino is Professor of Music and Sound Studies at Cornell University. Her publications include articles on medieval music, Blondie, David Bowie, PJ Harvey, Mick Jagger, Lou Reed, and Pussy Riot; and the books Listening to the Sirens: Musical Technologies of Queer Identity from Homer to Hedwig, and Giving Voice to Love: Song and Self-Expression from the Troubadours to Guillaume de Machaut. She is co-author (with Tom McEnaney) of We’re Having Much More Fun: Punk Archives for the Present from CBGB to Gilman and Beyond. Tom Enaney (Associate Professor of Comparative Literature and Spanish & Portuguese, UC Berkeley) writes about sonic media, music, and literature from the Caribbean, Latin America, and the United States. He is the author of Acoustic Properties: Radio, Narrative, and the New Neighborhood of the Americas (2017), and many articles in venues like diacritics, the Journal of Musicology, PMLA, Representations, and Revista de estudios hispánicos. He is an Associate Professor in the departments of Comparative Literature and Spanish & Portuguese, and craiglist Distinguished Chair in New Media at UC Berkeley, as well as co-director of the UC-Cuba Academic Initiative. Anna Joy Springer (she, they) is a lifelong Californian whose artistic work uses fantastical, speculative, and other figurative modes to explore the nature of interbeing and to register lesser cultural currents through writing and pictures. She is author of The Birdwisher, The Vicious Red Relic, Love, and The Forests of the Vicious Red Relic, Love: A Companion to the Memoir, along with other publications across genres. Frontwoman of former punk bands Blatz, The Gr’ups, and Cypher in the Snow, Anna Joy’s hardcore full-throated feminism inflects a wildly responsive performance style that’s saturated in femme camp, intellectual reflexivity, and political outrage. Anna Joy widely toured the U.S. and Europe in the 1990’s in her bands and as a member of Sister Spit, a queer feminist troupe of writers. Records featuring her bands and literary projects are available on digital platforms, CD, and vinyl. Currently an Associate Professor of Literature at the University of California, San Diego, Anna Joy got a B.A. in Humanities from New College of California with support from a Pell Grant and continued her education at Brown University, where she was awarded an M.F.A. in Literary Arts (Fiction) as well as the John Assatly Memorial Award in Fiction and the Weston Family Prize in Creative Writing, Fiction. Deeply influenced by student-centered social justice pedagogies, Anna Joy helped design and direct UCSD’s cross-genre MFA program in literary arts, receiving a Distinguished Teaching Award for excellence in instruction. She’s also the recipient of Chancellor's Associates Faculty Excellence Award for Excellence in Performing and Visual Arts, two fellowship awards from the Hellman Foundation, and a Dean’s Innovation Award. Both in the academy and in other settings, she teaches a wide range of writing, graphic texts, and embodied mindfulness courses incorporating over twenty years of experience as professional writing instructor. Anna Joy is student of both Zen and Theravadan Buddhist practices. Birds and bird symbology remain favorite subjects, so Anna Joy is grateful to live with her beloved and many pets in Southern California, surrounded by woodpeckers and screech owls. Our events are FREE and open to the public!

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... London: printed by the author, 1671. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: Commercialization Clinic
description: Commercialization Clinic Are you a builder, researcher, and founder who is ready to think seriously about commercialization, but not sure where to start? The Commercialization Clinic is an open, conversational space hosted by Anthony Reza Razavi once a month to drop in and explore the questions that matter most: When is the right time to file for IP protection?How does publishing impact my ability to secure IP protection?How do I bridge the gap between lab proof-of-concept and industry-ready prototype?How can I clearly differentiate my solution from existing alternatives?What types of partnerships could accelerate commercialization?How do I decide between licensing my technology to an existing company vs. forming a startup?How do I know if I’m “investor-ready”?What milestones make a technology attractive for licensing or acquisition?Surrounded by a curated collection of standout patents—hand-selected by the university's own commercialization team—you’ll be immersed in real examples of ideas that made the leap from concept to impact. What to Expect This isn’t a lecture. It’s a working session. Bring your ideas, early-stage inventions, or half-formed questions. Whether you're refining a disclosure, exploring startup pathways, or simply trying to understand how intellectual property fits into your work, this monthly clinic was designed to help you on your startup journey. You’ll walk away with: Clearer next steps on patents and IP strategyInsight into how commercialization actually unfoldsPractical guidance grounded in real industry and academic experienceMeet Your Host At the intersection of discovery and deployment, Anthony Reza Razavi leads the Life Sciences Innovation team at UC San Diego, bringing a rare combination of scientific expertise and commercialization experience. He has a diverse background as a scientist, business development and operations professional in pharmaceutical industry, startups and as a tech transfer and corporate partnership professional in academia. He worked previously at the Foundation Venture Capital Group, where he gained experience in the investment and management of Startups in the Life Sciences. Clinic Details The Commercialization Clinic hosted by Anthony Reza Rezavi at the Patent Studio is open once a month for the following office hours: WHEN: Second Thursday of the Month | 3-5 p.m. WHERE: Design & Innovation Building, Patent Studio, Room 451 No appointments necesary. Drop-ins welcome! What is the Patent Studio? Located in the Entrepreneurship Center in Room 451, the Patent Studio is a curated environment built to inspire commercialization thinking. The patents on display there aren’t random; they’re selected to spark ideas, challenge assumptions, and show what’s possible when innovation is protected and positioned effectively. Discover what intellectual property looks like up close. Hours are limited, so please first check with Anthony Reza Rezavi before stopping by.

title: SIMPLY INA
description: An Evening Conversation with Ina Garten An evening onstage with Ina Garten—the beloved cookbook author and television host known to millions as the Barefoot Contessa—offers audiences the chance to hear from one of America’s most trusted voices in home cooking and hospitality. The evening will spotlight her new cookbook, Simply Ina (Clarkson Potter, October 2026), a vibrant collection of recipes that prove the most delicious cooking is often the simplest. For more than two decades, Garten has inspired home cooks with her signature blend of warmth, elegance, and practicality. A #1 New York Times bestselling author and longtime star of Food Network, she is the creator of more than a dozen bestselling cookbooks and the host of Be My Guest with Ina Garten. Her work has earned five Emmy Awards and two James Beard Awards, and her recipes have become staples in kitchens across the country. In conversation onstage, Garten will reflect on the remarkable path that brought her from running a small specialty food shop in the Hamptons to becoming one of the most recognizable culinary personalities in the world. With humor and candor, she’ll share stories from behind the scenes of her cookbooks and television shows, and discuss how her philosophy of approachable elegance—beautiful food made with confidence and ease—has shaped her career and her connection with generations of home cooks. Garten’s newest cookbook, Simply Ina, is a vibrant collection of 85 recipes designed to deliver maximum flavor with minimal effort. From make-ahead lunches and effortless appetizers to satisfying dinners and irresistible desserts, the book celebrates a guiding idea that has long defined Garten’s cooking: the best meals are often the simplest. Audiences will also hear about the practical wisdom and joyful spirit that define her work—her favorite time-saving strategies, her famously pragmatic “store-bought is fine” philosophy, and the creative thinking behind dishes like Mashed Potato & Leek Soup, make-ahead Provençal Chicken with Olives & Capers, and Cherry Berry Crumble. Ultimately, the evening celebrates the core message at the center of Garten’s cooking: that time in the kitchen should bring people together. With warmth, humor, and hard-won culinary insight, Ina Garten will remind us that simple food, made with care, can make life—and time around the table with the people you love—even more delicious.

description: GRIM is an irreverent, hilarious and heartbreaking world premiere musical that celebrates life… and death. After 300,000 years collecting souls, the Grim Reaper is retiring and his daughter Diana must pass a simple test to take over. title: Collage Poetry Exhibition Donation Drive
description: Do you have old magazines, vintage zines, or leftover craft supplies? We are gathering materials for a community Collage Poetry project that will be turned into a public exhibition. What is Collage Poetry? Collage Poetry weaves together existing text and visual fragments such as magazine cutouts, newspaper snippets, book jackets, zines, school reports/papers, and even non-paper materials (yarn, ribbon, glitter) to form a new, layered work of art. Check out examples from the Alice Notley Artworks collection, like Alone - I Pour a Cup or Vacuum. What to Donate: We are seeking materials in any language, including: Magazines and newspapersBook jackets and zinesOld school reports or papersMixed media (yarn, ribbon, fabric scraps, etc.)Where to Donate: Donations can be dropped off at the collection boxes located in the Service Hubs at Geisel Library and WongAvery Library during each building’s open hours. View Geisel’s hoursView WongAvery’s hours (note: WongAvery is closed on Saturdays)Note: All donations are final and will not be returned. Please ensure all donated papers, reports, or documents are free of sensitive or personal information. We kindly ask that all donations be clean and free of mold, odors, or pests. For safety reasons, please do not donate hazardous materials, including broken glass, chemicals, or sharp metal objects. Questions? Contact us at ucsdlibrary@ucsd.edu.

title: Shaping a Library | Exhibition
description: In early 1970, a San Diego newspaper announced, “Unique Library Taking Shape.” The headline referred to UC San Diego’s Central University Library, now Geisel Library, which was then under construction. The Library’s story began several years earlier. In 1965, architect William L. Pereira was invited to design the Central University Library, envisioned as the flagship building for the UC San Diego campus. Construction began in 1968, and by September 1971, the new Central University Library was dedicated. Over the decades, the building has continued to evolve through expansions and renovations, adapting to the changing needs of the campus community. Tracing the history of the Library’s site design process, construction and expansion from 1965 to 1993, Shaping a Library draws on unique materials from UC San Diego Library’s Special Collections & Archives. From Pereira’s original spherical concept for Geisel Library to Gunnar Birkerts’ glass-walled expansion, architectural drawings, photographs and documents reveal the ideas, people and processes that shaped this beloved campus landmark. Shaping a Library is on view in the Exhibition Gallery on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours from Saturday, September 26 through Tuesday, December 8, 2026. Can’t make it to campus to view the exhibition in-person? View the digital exhibit. Image Credit: Architectural rendering of UC San Diego Central University Library, William L. Pereira and Associates, 1965. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.

title: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature | Exhibit
description: The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is an annual art and literary magazine created by medical students for the UC San Diego School of Medicine community. Now in its 32nd year, the student-led publication features art, photography, poetry, prose, sculpture, comics and more, providing a space for safe expression, creativity and exploring identities beyond medicine. This exhibition presents selected works from the 2025 and 2026 issues, offering a glimpse into the experiences, perspectives and creative lives of the School of Medicine community. Visitors are invited to pause, reflect and explore the many dimensions of the human experience. The Human Condition: An Exploration of Art & Literature is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from September 26 to December 13, 2026, during the building's open hours. Previous issues of The Human Condition magazine, dating back to 2007-08, are available to download and read at your leisure. Curated by: Amy Xue, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27 Myat Wai, MS4, editor-in-chief, 2026-27Supported by: UC San Diego School of MedicineUC San Diego Library

title: UC San Diego Horizon x Techstars Startup Weekend: Justice + AI
description: UC San Diego's Design and Innovation Building hosts Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego, bringing builders, designers, lawyers, and the legally curious together for a weekend focused squarely on legal tech, software, and innovation. The theme: reimagining law for the AI era. The legal industry touches nearly everyone and has changed less than almost any other sector in the last few decades — this weekend is about building the tools that could finally change that, from AI that helps a tenant fight an eviction to software that lets a small business draft a contract without a $400-an-hour phone call. ​Around 100 participants will pitch ideas, form teams around the strongest ones, and spend the weekend building toward a final pitch to a panel of judges. Mentors and coaches work alongside teams throughout, helping them get out of the building to validate ideas with real users, sharpen product direction, and prepare a polished final pitch. ​Julian Bryant, Lead Organizer of Techstars Startup Weekend San Diego and an attorney/software developer himself, has facilitated roughly 40 Startup Weekends and brings a track record of real companies launched from the format — including CreativeUp, a Santa Barbara-based company that formed at one of his earliest events and is still operating more than six years later. ​Jacques Chirazi, Director of the Basement and Entrepreneurship Center at UC San Diego's Office of Innovation and Commercialization, brings UC San Diego's student entrepreneurship ecosystem into the weekend, connecting participants to campus resources that can carry momentum well past Sunday night. ​Mason Baldwin: TBD ​This isn't just a competition — it's an entrepreneurial laboratory. Participants who've never attempted a startup get to try on different roles — founder, designer, engineer — and learn by doing what Julian calls "experiential education entrepreneurship," packed into three days.

Image taken from "A Map to the Next World" by 2019-2022 Poet Laureate Joy Harjo. Harjo was the first Native American Poet Laureate and centered her term on celebrating indigenous poetry and voices with her project "Living Nations, Living Worlds."

title: Library Milestones | Exhibit
description: Before the rise of digital publications and licensed electronic resources, academic libraries measured the size of their collections by the number of physical volumes on their shelves. Reaching a million-volume milestone was a source of pride and a mark of growth. This exhibit highlights five titles that mark milestones in the growth of the UC San Diego Library’s physical collections. Together, they also reflect the generosity of donors and support groups who helped build the collections and offer a glimpse into what made a book milestone-worthy at the time. Library Milestones is on view outside of Special Collections & Archives on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library during the building's open hours through Sunday, December 13, 2026. Photo citation: John Ogilby. America: being the latest, and most accurate description of the New World; containing the original inhabitants, and the remarkable voyages thither... London: printed by the author, 1671. UC San Diego Library, Special Collections & Archives.
